01.r: Melchizedek's blessing turns from Abram to God.
01.n: A passive participle, 'blessed', with no verb 'be'. It can be read as a wish ('blessed be') or a statement ('blessed is', as YLT has it). Gesenius puts 'to bend the knees, to kneel' first among this verb's senses; BDB lists 'bless God, adore with bended knees'.

02.r: God, named with the short word El.
02.n: This is El, not the usual plural form for God. Gesenius gives its root sense as strong, mighty, a mighty one.

03.r: A title of God: the one above all.
03.n: Gesenius gives the adjective's first sense as high, higher, of a place, and then supreme; BDB: Highest, Most High, as a name of God.

04.n: The DRC rewords the clause around 'by whose protection'.

05.r: God gave Abram's enemies into his power.
05.n: A rare verb, in only three verses. Gesenius says it is not used in the simple form and gives this form as TO GIVE, TO DELIVER, citing Gen. 14:20. The DRC's 'by whose protection' probably reads the consonants as the noun for 'shield', which is spelled the same; that is an inference.

06.r: The kings Abram had just defeated.
06.n: The brief's lexicon gives adversary, foe, enemy, oppressor. YLT's 'adversaries' is the closest of the translations.

07.n: Literally 'in your hand'; with a verb of handing over, English says 'into'. The brief's lexicon lists strength, power as a figurative sense of 'hand'.

08.n: The Hebrew does not name the giver or the receiver: only 'he gave him'. The context makes Abram the giver and Melchizedek the receiver, which is how the Geneva and BSB read it; that is an inference from the story, not stated in this verse.

10.r: A tenth part, given as a tithe.
10.n: Gesenius gives 'tithes' and cites this verse; the brief's lexicon gives tithe, tenth part. The newer translations here say 'a tenth'; this edition keeps 'tithe' for this noun and 'tenth' for the plain number.

11.r: Out of all he had, most likely the recovered goods.
11.n: Literally 'from all'. What 'all' covers is not said here; that it means the goods recovered in the battle is a reasonable reading of the story.

01.n: εὐλογητός, 'blessed', the adjective used of God.

05.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. παραδίδωμι, 'hand over'.

07.n: ὑποχείριος, 'under the hand': 'handed over your enemies as subject to you'.

10.n: δεκάτη, 'a tenth', the Greek word for the tenth part.
